text:
nadir: heads up 10 mins of weird static on calls this morning. turned out to be my vintage tabletop radio sitting behind the router. unplugged it and calls cleared up. image: (radio-next-to-router.jpg)
keisha: vintage radio? that's surprisingly plausible. old transformers can be noisy.
pete: did it start broadcasting an SSID called RADIO_RUIN? :rofl:
nadir: no SSID, just intermittent hiss/pings. infra checks showed latency spike exactly when i turned the radio on.
maya: timeline: wifi poor -> unplug radio -> instant recovery. classic.
ops-bot: diagnostic run by nadir at 2165010005 10s ping to staging pre-unplug avg=214ms loss=7% ; post-unplug avg=18ms loss=0%. logs posted to #eng-infra.
monitor-bot: auto-note: if you have legacy electronics near your router consider moving them 1-2ft. ferrite core suggestion: https://example.com/ferrite-guide
keisha: poll idea: "weirdest vintage item that killed my wifi" thread tomorrow? winners get bragging rights.
pete: i'm in. i've got a lava lamp and an industrial desk fan in my arsenal.
maya: i'll bring my space heater that acts like a tiny jammer. not proud.
nadir: i'll post a close-up radio pic and my duct-tape cable fort. who will actually tidy before posting? :stuck_out_tongue_winking_eye:
participants poll replies: nadir: maybe, keisha: nope, pete: no, maya: yes
